## Overview

The code in this script uses the cohort of kidney transplant patients with and without cryptococcosis developed in the [`R/create_cohort.R`](create_cohort.qmd)
and executes 1:n matching based on a custom-written greedy algorithm

Characteristics of the matching algorithm:

- **Matching without replacement:** [each patient without cryptococcosis serves as a control to at most one case]{.pending}, which keeps the later analysis simpler [@stuart2010matching].
- **Risk-set sampling (incidence density sampling):** if a case develops cryptococcosis 243 days after their most recent kidney transplant, potential controls are chosen on their covariate values at exactly 243 days after their own most recent transplant [@richardson2004incidence].
- **Greedy matching:** each case's controls are chosen in turn, and earlier choices are not revisited [@austin2014algorithms]. Cases are taken in order of how few potential controls they have, a choice made in this code; the order of greedy matching has at most a modest effect on estimates [@austin2014algorithms].
- **Mix of exact matching and caliper matching**
  - Exact matching on the following:
    - Cirrhosis
    - HIV
    - Diabetes
  - Caliper matching on the following:
    - Age (within 10 years on the index date, calculated exactly)
    - Index date of case and controls (within 3 years of each other)
  - Preferential matching on the following:
    - Number of transplants prior to index date 

**Decision pending:** whether a person may serve as a control in more than one risk set ([D4](analysis-plan.qmd#13-open-decisions)).

**Current code:** potential controls are limited to patients never diagnosed with cryptococcosis, so people diagnosed later cannot serve as controls before their diagnosis ([#7](https://github.com/VagishHemmige/Cryptococcus-cost-analysis/issues/7)). Other differences from the plan, including the order in which cases are matched, are listed under [Cases and controls](study_cases_controls.qmd#what-cases-and-controls-are-matched-on).
